craft_claim: Sustained high foregrounding and ornament fatigue the reader and lower fluency, so the lyrical voice must alternate with plain prose and yield at argument, information, and stakes peaks.

supporting_evidence.note: Processing ease yields positive affect; effortful disfluency lowers it, implying a ceiling on ornament density beyond which the tone becomes counterproductive.
Foregrounding only registers against a background of ordinary language, so lyrical passages require intervening plain prose to remain perceptible.

supporting_evidence.location: On Repeat (Oxford University Press), on repetition and attention
supporting_evidence.note: Repetition's musical effect depends on spacing and context; too-frequent repetition or refrain loses its force.

counterevidence.note: Some readers tolerate and even seek sustained foregrounding, so the threshold is a craft default, not a psychological absolute.

scope: Long-form prose, serial content, academic and informational writing, and any passage that must remain clear.
exceptions: Short lyric forms (a poem, an invocation, a coda) may sustain the register for their whole span.
